title: Standards, structure, settings and memory
outcome: A project runs on one foundation. Everything is built on the ICE model with written standards, the structure says where everything lives, settings hold what can be turned on or off, agents decide from three tiers of memory, and each part runs on the right model. Teams can build their own harness on it.
why: Agents follow the rules and memory they're given, so a loose rule or a wrong page reaches every later decision.
proof: The checks hold every part to the standard.
Nothing an agent decides from sits outside memory.
must_not: Name a tracker in a play, skill or sub-agent, because they only know the tool.

touches.title: Standards
Keep one written harness standard, with its parts, its principles and how it is kept
Record each change to the standard as a decision, with what it replaces
Build every play and loop from its ICE, and keep the compiled part matched to it
Follow a written standard for each kind of part: play, loop, sub-agent, skill, script, shared file and tool
Name every part by one rule, with five roles owning the verbs
Map every old name to its new one, and check that no old name is left
Rename the harness plays and the loop to the standard
Rename the change, plan, knowledge and record plays to the standard
Rename the lifecycle and lens plays to the standard
Rename the skills to the standard
Check every part against the standard
Hold every part to the rules all parts follow: asking a person, staying on scope, the way of working, and no client or personal reference
Give every finding and defect one severity, P1 to P4
Check that no play, skill or sub-agent names a tracker
Build your own harness
Build a play from its ICE
Change a play through its ICE
Build a loop from its ICE
Change a loop through its ICE
Check a loop against the loop principles, including what starts it
Add a gate to a play with its way past, and pin or unpin one
Mark that a play is running, so a guardrail can tell a play's work from a shortcut
Build a sub-agent and a skill to the standard
Build a harness in a team's own repository, against a written architecture
Structure
Lay out Garura's source: where each kind of part, tool, memory and setting lives
Lay out an installed project: where each part lands, the shared files, the tools and the memory guide
Keep `.garura/` to its written list, and check it
Keep each run's records with its issue, with only repository paths in them
Settings
Keep every setting in one settings file, laid as each project's copy
Say what each setting means and who reads it, and fail a setting no one reads
Keep every other settings file in one folder
Turn each checkpoint on or off, and keep the policy learned from a person's answers
Turn a run's evidence on or off

Hold the settings other capabilities need: the test model, the design settings, the kinds of change that may go ahead on their own, the connections, the review rounds, the question tier, the loop settings and the trackers
Make every tool read its settings
Memory
Find memory across three tiers through one tool
Let only a person decide a memory update, one at a time
Keep each decision's trace and check its sources
Make every agent read memory only through the tool, and fail a part that names a memory path
Keep Phoenix memory in step with Garura's source, versioned per release with its notes
Bring Phoenix memory to a machine and keep it current
Move a page up a tier on a person's yes, and choose what is learned
Check what memory holds: pages out of date, sources that changed
Keep what agents decide from inside memory: the machine-wide copy, Claude Code's own memory, and the rules
Intelligent model routing
Give each part a model tier and an effort by a written rule
Send a step to the model a setting names, apart from the session's
Record each run's model, effort, time and cost for each part
Move a part up or down a tier on that record, and check the move with an eval
Choose the model and effort by the job at run time
